# Lawyer Standard Operating Procedure
## Demanding Evidence
On [bold]Code Green[/bold] you [bold]must[/bold] demand the evidence behind any charge brought against your client, and Security is expected to produce it. A charge whose basis you cannot see is a charge you are obliged to contest.
Test it against the standard: findings must be matched to your client, printed, and reach the score set out in [textlink="Legal SOP" link="GuideLegalSOP"]. Presence at a scene is not a case.
A warrant is only valid if signed by the [bold]relevant department head, or the highest-ranking command staff[/bold] - the Captain in most cases. An implant search also needs the Chief Medical Officer. One signed by anybody else is not valid.
## Case Files
Seek out the findings the Detective has gathered, take copies for your client, and store them.
Keep one file per client. Evidence you never copied cannot be produced later, and a copy you did not take is a copy that can be amended without you.
## Faxing Central Command
Where you believe a charge is false, or that a warrant was improperly issued or signed, [bold]fax Central Command[/bold] with the details.
Do this as well as raising it with command, not instead of it. The fax is the record that outlasts the shift.
[italic]See [textlink="Detective SOP" link="GuideDetectiveSOP"] for how findings are meant to be stored, and [textlink="Space Law" link="SpaceLaw"] for your client's rights while confined.[/italic]
